text:
maya: Heads up — multiple customers reporting reconnect storms and weird routing after yesterday's proxy canary. Seeing a lot of short-lived streams that immediately reconnect.

sam: Same. Console shows a spike in 'route:unknown' for streaming sessions, and cost jump on the ingress side. Not all requests have trace ids. :thinking:

devon: I dug into logs. Probe connections (we append ?probe=true for session health probes) are coming through with trace headers stripped. Example from the proxy access log dump:headers: { traceparent: null, x-rw-session: "abc123", user-agent: "probe/1.0" }

maya: That explains missing telemetry. If traceparent is stripped, the console attributes those spans to default/unknown and routing fallbacks kick in.

lee: Any idea which change could strip trace headers? The proxy config PR we rolled (PR #4523) added a header sanitization rule for caching endpoints.

devon: Yup — PR #4523 added remove_headers: [traceparent, tracestate] for paths that looked cacheable. But our probe path looks like /stream?probe=true and matched the rule. Oops.

priya: When traceparent is missing, routing goes through the fallback path that doesn't preserve sticky shard id -> client gets routed to different backend, server sees it as new session and consumes another token. That explains duplicate token consumption.

maya: Urgent ask: can we pause the canary of that proxy change? ops-bot: FYI.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary for proxy-v2 paused at 12% (manual pause requested by maya).

sam: Quick mitigation: patch the rule to ignore query param probe=true OR narrow match to only /static/* paths. Which is faster?

devon: Fastest is to toggle the header sanitization to exclude requests with ?probe=true. I can push a hotfix to the canary config in 15m. Patch looks like:- match: path_prefix: /stream
  headers:
    - name: ":query"
      exact_match: "probe=true"
  remove_headers: []

lee: Also want a small console dashboard tile showing stream.missing_trace_count so we spot regressions earlier. Can we emit a metric when traceparent is missing?

devon: I can add a guard in the ingress to increment stream.missing_trace counter when probe=true or when header absent. Low cost.

priya: Follow-up: we should also make routing decision not to fall back to round-robin when x-rw-session exists but trace is missing — preserve sticky route if session cookie is present. That avoids double token use.

maya: Agreed. Short-term: devon hotfix the proxy rule. medium-term: add metric + dashboard + routing guard. long-term: audit header sanitization rules.

sam: Logging commands for others: rg "probe=true" infra/logs | jq '.headers | {traceparent, tracestate, x-rw-session}' — shows offenders.

devon: Patch pushed to canary config, rolling to the paused hosts now. Monitoring: watch stream.reconnect_rate and stream.missing_trace for 30m.

ops-bot: alert: deploy success to canary hosts (5/40).

lee: Adding temporary dashboard tile and alert: alert if stream.missing_trace > 50/min over 5m — will notify #eng-oncall.

priya: Created GH issue RW-7890 to track sticky-routing fallback change + postmortem.

maya: Thanks team. Once metrics look stable, schedule a config audit. :thumbsup:

sam: Noted — I'll monitor billing-side for duplicate token consumption and update ops-CS if customers need credits.

devon: Quick note: check for other header-sanitization rules that use broad path prefixes. I found one that targeted / earlier; will narrow them all.

maya: Closing loop in 60m with status update. :eyes:
